questions.heading: A Dimension Accumulates a Quantity Along Each Route
questions.stem: Three vans leave a depot with a Distance dimension whose start cumuls are fixed at 0 and whose global span coefficient is 50. Their routes are 40, 55 and 70 km. What does the span term add to the objective?

options.text: 50 times 165, the sum of the three routes
options.says: The span is the largest end cumul minus the smallest start cumul, not the sum of the routes.

options.text: 50 times 30, the longest route minus the shortest
options.says: The span subtracts the smallest start cumul, which is 0 here, not the shortest route.

options.text: 50 times 70, the longest route minus a start of 0
options.says: Right: global span = largest end cumul − smallest start cumul = 70 − 0.

options.text: Nothing, since a dimension only ever limits its cumuls
options.says: A dimension is a constraint by default, but SetGlobalSpanCostCoefficient adds a cost to the objective.

questions.heading: A Capacity Is a Dimension Whose Transit Is the Demand
questions.stem: A truck's Load dimension uses a unary demand callback. Its route is depot, A (demand 4), B (demand 6), C (demand 3), depot. What is the Load cumul at B?

options.text: 4, the load picked up before the truck arrives at B
options.says: Right: the cumul is the value on arrival; B's own demand is added on the arc that leaves B.

options.text: 10, the load once B's own demand has been picked up
options.says: B's demand is the transit of the arc leaving B, so it shows at C, not at B.

options.text: 6, the demand that B itself adds to the truck's load
options.says: The cumul is the running total on arrival, not one stop's demand.

options.text: 13, the whole route's load, fixed for every stop
options.says: 13 is the cumul at the route's end; at each stop the cumul is what was picked up before it.

questions.heading: The Search Does Not Prove That a Fleet Is Too Small
questions.stem: A planner's routing model with 5 trucks and a 10-second time limit returns None, and routing.status() names ROUTING_FAIL_TIMEOUT. What can the planner conclude?

options.text: No routes exist for 5 trucks, so the model is proven infeasible
options.says: Infeasibility would be ROUTING_INFEASIBLE; a timeout only says no routes were found in time.

options.text: Routes exist, since the status would say INFEASIBLE if they did not
options.says: The search rarely proves infeasibility; the lesson's 2-crew fleet could not fit and still got FAIL_TIMEOUT.

options.text: The trucks are always too few, so a sixth truck must be added
options.says: A timeout says nothing about why; the data or the search may be at fault.

options.text: The search found nothing in time, which is no proof either way
options.says: Right: FAIL_TIMEOUT means the limit came before any routes; check demand against capacity yourself.
